operation: the taking of refuge in God, who is a shield to all who do so — the reliance that shelters in God and his ever-true word, finding him a proven protection
target: (God the shield in whom refuge is taken)
coupling: the trust that flees to God for shelter and is not disappointed
reading: chasah (take refuge/shelter) — 'he is a shield to those who TAKE REFUGE in him' (30:5); God's word is flawless and he himself a shield to those who trust him. To take refuge in God is to be sheltered by a proven, faithful protection (cf 18:10; Ps 18:30).
verse_text: Pro 30:5 Every word of God proves true ; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him .

read_sense_variants: presumption — tampering with revelation, exposed as falsehood
sense: presumption — tampering with revelation, exposed as falsehood
operation: the being found a liar for adding to God's words — the presumption that tampers with or supplements divine revelation, exposed as falsehood when God rebukes it
target: (the true word it dares to add to)
coupling: the arrogance of amending God's flawless word, unmasked as a lie
reading: kazab (lie/falsehood) — 'do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a LIAR' (30:6); to supplement or tamper with God's flawless word is presumption that God exposes as falsehood. Revelation is not ours to amend (cf Deut 4:2; Rev 22:18-19).
verse_text: Pro 30:6 Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar.

read_sense_variants: humble request — asking two things of God before death
sense: humble request — asking two things of God before death
operation: the asking of two things of God before death — Agur's humble, earnest petition, a prayer that knows its own need and lays two specific requests before God with reverent urgency
coupling: the humble, self-knowing prayer that asks God for what the soul truly needs
reading: shaal (ask/request) — 'two things I ASK of you; deny them not to me before I die' (30:7); Agur prays with humble, urgent specificity. His is a prayer that knows its own weakness and asks God to guard it — the model of self-knowing petition (30:8-9).
verse_text: Pro 30:7 Two things I ask of you; deny them not to me before I die :

read_sense_variants: riches — among Wisdom's endowments | riches — grasped by the violent | contentment — the prayer for sufficiency, wanting neither want nor wealth
sense: contentment — the prayer for sufficiency, wanting neither want nor wealth
operation: the desire for neither poverty nor riches but only one's needful food — the contentment that prays to be spared both extremes, wanting neither the want that tempts to theft nor the wealth that tempts to deny God, asking only for enough
target: (the falsehood he also prays to be spared)
coupling: the contented spirit that asks only for sufficiency, fearing the perils of both want and wealth
reading: osher (riches) — 'give me neither poverty nor RICHES; feed me with the food that is needful for me' (30:8); the prayer of contentment. Agur asks to be spared both extremes, knowing wealth tempts to deny God and want to steal (30:9). To desire only enough is a rare and wise contentment (cf 1 Tim 6:8).
verse_text: Pro 30:8 Remove far from me falsehood and lying ; give me neither poverty nor riches ; feed me with the food that is needful for me,

read_sense_variants: self-sufficient forgetting — the satiety that denies God, 'who is the LORD?'
sense: self-sufficient forgetting — the satiety that denies God, 'who is the LORD?'
operation: the denying of God in plenty — the danger that satiety breeds self-sufficient forgetting, so that the full man says 'who is the LORD?', needing God no longer in his own eyes
target: the theft of want it is set against (267322)
coupling: set against the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name
reading: kachash (deny/deceive) — 'lest I be FULL and DENY you and say, 'who is the LORD?'' (30:9); prosperity tempts a man to self-sufficient forgetting of God. Agur prays against riches lest plenty make him deny his Maker (cf Deut 8:12-14).
verse_text: Pro 30:9 lest I be full and deny you and say , “ Who is the Lord ?” or lest I be poor and steal and profane the name of my God .

read_sense_variants: desperation-sin — the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name
sense: desperation-sin — the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name
operation: the stealing that poverty may drive a man to, profaning the name of his God — the danger that want breeds desperation-sin, dishonouring God by the theft it provokes
target: the denial of plenty it is set against (267316)
coupling: set against the satiety that denies God
reading: ganab (steal) — 'or lest I be poor and STEAL and profane the name of my God' (30:9); poverty too has its spiritual peril, driving a man to theft that shames God. Agur prays against want no less than wealth. Emergent: desperation-sin as the danger of poverty (cf 6:30-31).
verse_text: Pro 30:9 lest I be full and deny you and say , “ Who is the Lord ?” or lest I be poor and steal and profane the name of my God .

read_sense_variants: malicious tale-bearing — accusing a servant to his master, and incurring guilt
sense: malicious tale-bearing — accusing a servant to his master, and incurring guilt
operation: the slandering of a servant to his master — malicious tale-bearing against one who cannot easily defend himself, which recoils in a curse and guilt on the slanderer
target: (the guilt it brings on the slanderer)
coupling: the malicious accusation that rebounds on the one who makes it
reading: lashan (slander/accuse) — 'do not SLANDER a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty' (30:10); malicious accusation, especially of the lowly, brings guilt on the accuser. To injure a servant with the tongue is to court a curse (cf 6:16-19).
verse_text: Pro 30:10 Do not slander a servant to his master , lest he curse you, and you be held guilty .

read_sense_variants: filial impiety — the generation that curses its father and will not bless its mother
sense: filial impiety — the generation that curses its father and will not bless its mother
operation: the impiety of a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother — the contempt for parents that heads Agur's portrait of a corrupt generation, honour owed and withheld
coupling: the contempt for father and mother that marks a corrupt generation
reading: barak (bless), negated + curse — 'there are those who curse their fathers and do not BLESS their mothers' (30:11); the first mark of a wicked generation is contempt for parents. To curse a father and withhold blessing from a mother is a foundational impiety (cf 20:20; 30:17; Ex 21:17).
verse_text: Pro 30:11 There are those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers .

read_sense_variants: self-righteous self-deception — thinking oneself pure while unwashed of filth
sense: self-righteous self-deception — thinking oneself pure while unwashed of filth
operation: the being 'clean in one's own eyes' while unwashed of one's filth — the self-righteous self-deception that congratulates itself on a purity it does not have, blind to its own defilement
target: (the unwashed filth it will not see)
coupling: the self-flattering blindness that mistakes its own filth for cleanness
reading: tahor (clean/pure), self-assessed — 'there are those who are CLEAN in their own eyes but are not washed of their filth' (30:12); the second mark of a corrupt generation is self-righteous self-deception — a purity claimed, not real. The heart most defiled may be surest of its own cleanness (cf 16:2; 20:9; Luke 18:11).
verse_text: Pro 30:12 There are those who are clean in their own eyes but are not washed of their filth .

read_sense_variants: rapacious cruelty — teeth like swords, consuming the poor and needy
sense: rapacious cruelty — teeth like swords, consuming the poor and needy
operation: the devouring of the poor and needy by those whose teeth are swords and fangs knives — the rapacious cruelty that consumes the weak off the earth, greed turned predator upon the helpless
coupling: the predatory cruelty that eats up the defenceless
reading: akal (eat/devour) — 'to DEVOUR the poor from off the earth, the needy from among mankind' (30:14); the last mark of a corrupt generation is rapacious cruelty — greed with a predator's teeth, consuming the weak. Emergent: oppression as devouring, the wicked feeding on the poor (cf 28:15; Ps 14:4; Amos 8:4).
verse_text: Pro 30:14 There are those whose teeth are swords, whose fangs are knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, the needy from among mankind.

read_sense_variants: satisfaction — filled with good from the fruit of one's mouth | satisfaction — filled by the fruit of one's own mouth | satisfaction — the harvest of one's own lips | unsatisfied craving — the eyes of man that never have enough | insatiable craving — the greed that, like the leech, never says 'Enough'
sense: insatiable craving — the greed that, like the leech, never says 'Enough'
operation: the never-being-satisfied of the leech's daughters ('Give, Give') and the four insatiable things — an image of greed and craving that, like Sheol and fire, can never be filled and never says 'Enough'
target: (the four insatiables it is likened to)
coupling: the bottomless appetite that no amount of getting ever contents
reading: saba (be satisfied), negated — 'the leech has two daughters: Give and Give... never SATISFIED... never say, 'Enough'' (30:15-16); greed is bottomless, insatiable as the grave, the barren womb, the parched land, and fire. Craving is a hunger nothing fills (cf 27:20; Eccl 5:10).
verse_text: Pro 30:15 The leech has two daughters : Give and Give . Three things are never satisfied ; four never say , “ Enough ”:

read_sense_variants: to mock/deride — Wisdom's answering derision at their calamity | mockery — mocking the poor, which insults God | filial derision — the eye that mocks its father
sense: filial derision — the eye that mocks its father
operation: the mocking of a father with the eye — the derision of a parent that, with scorn for a mother's authority, draws a terrible judgement, contempt for the parents who gave one life
target: the scorn of the mother it is joined with (267134)
coupling: welded to the scorning of a mother's authority
reading: laag (mock/deride) — 'the eye that MOCKS a father' (30:17); to deride one's father is a grievous impiety, judged with horror (the corpse left for ravens). Contempt for parents is contempt for the source of one's life (cf 30:11; 20:20).
verse_text: Pro 30:17 The eye that mocks a father and scorns to obey a mother will be picked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by the vultures .

read_sense_variants: filial contempt — scorning obedience to a mother
sense: filial contempt — scorning obedience to a mother
operation: the scorning to obey a mother — the contempt for maternal authority that, with mockery of a father, marks the rebellious child on whom a fearful judgement falls
target: the mockery of the father it is joined with (267132)
coupling: welded to the eye that mocks a father
reading: buz (despise/scorn) — 'and SCORNS to obey a mother' (30:17); contempt for a mother's authority, twin to mockery of a father, brings terrible judgement. To scorn the parents is to invite ruin.
verse_text: Pro 30:17 The eye that mocks a father and scorns to obey a mother will be picked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by the vultures .

read_sense_variants: reverent wonder — things too wonderful to grasp
sense: reverent wonder — things too wonderful to grasp
operation: the wonder Agur feels at things too wonderful for him — the reverent amazement before mysteries that exceed his grasp (the eagle's flight, the ship's course, the way of a man with a maid), humility that marvels rather than presumes
target: the acknowledged ignorance it goes with (267146)
coupling: welded to the not-understanding Agur openly confesses
reading: pala (be wonderful/beyond) — 'three things are too WONDERFUL for me' (30:18); the wise heart marvels at what it cannot fully grasp. Wonder before mystery is a mark of humility, not ignorance ashamed (cf 30:2-4).
verse_text: Pro 30:18 Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand :

read_sense_variants: owned mystery — Agur confessing four things he cannot understand
sense: owned mystery — Agur confessing four things he cannot understand
operation: the not-understanding that Agur confesses of the four wonderful things — the honest owning of mystery, refusing to pretend a comprehension he lacks, wonder joined to humble ignorance
coupling: welded to the reverent amazement Agur feels
reading: yada (know/understand), negated — 'four I do not UNDERSTAND' (30:18); Agur openly owns what he cannot comprehend. To confess the limits of one's understanding is wisdom, not failure (cf 30:2-3).
verse_text: Pro 30:18 Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand :

read_sense_variants: habitual adultery — sin grown as casual as a meal
sense: habitual adultery — sin grown as casual as a meal
operation: the way of the adulteress who eats, wipes her mouth, and says 'I have done no wrong' — habitual sin grown so casual that it is committed and dismissed as easily as a meal, no more troubling to the conscience
target: the brazen denial that accompanies it (267179)
coupling: welded to the seared conscience that denies all wrong
reading: naaph (commit adultery) — 'this is the way of an ADULTERESS'; habitual sin becomes as routine and untroubling as eating. The chilling ease with which she sins and dismisses it shows a conscience wholly seared (cf 5:6; 1 Tim 4:2).
verse_text: Pro 30:20 This is the way of an adulteress : she eats and wipes her mouth and says , “I have done no wrong .”

read_sense_variants: seared conscience — brazen denial of guilt after sin
sense: seared conscience — brazen denial of guilt after sin
operation: the saying 'I have done no wrong' after the deed — the brazen, self-acquitting denial of a conscience so seared that it feels no guilt, wiping the mouth as if nothing had happened
coupling: welded to the casual adultery it dismisses
reading: aven (wrong/iniquity), denied — 'and says, 'I have done no WRONG''; the deepest horror of habitual sin is not the deed but the untroubled conscience that denies it. Sin becomes invisible to the one hardened in it (cf 30:12; Jer 6:15).
verse_text: Pro 30:20 This is the way of an adulteress : she eats and wipes her mouth and says , “I have done no wrong .”

read_sense_variants: folly — the boor whom fine speech ill-suits | insufferable folly — the fool grown full and unbearable
sense: insufferable folly — the fool grown full and unbearable
operation: the fool when he is filled with food — folly given plenty and ease, so that it swells into something the earth can hardly bear, a fool with abundance being intolerable where a fool in want was merely pitiable
coupling: the folly that plenty makes insufferable
reading: nabal (fool) — 'a FOOL when he is filled with food'; one of the four things the earth cannot bear. A fool made comfortable and full grows insufferable — plenty gives folly power and removes its restraint (cf 1:32; 30:9).
verse_text: Pro 30:22 a slave when he becomes king, and a fool when he is filled with food;

read_sense_variants: wisdom — the wise son who gladdens his father | the wise one — the person of settled competence who still learns | the wise/sages — those whose words carry authority | wisdom — the wise, who inherit honor | self-wisdom — conceit forbidden | wisdom — the wise lay up knowledge | wisdom — the wise of heart who receives commandments | wisdom — the wise of heart whom the fool serves | wisdom — the soul-winner is wise | wisdom — who listens to counsel
sense: instinctive prudence — the great wisdom of small, weak creatures
operation: the exceeding wisdom of four small creatures — the instinctive prudence and foresight of the weak and lowly (ant, badger, locust, lizard) that shames the great, wisdom being a matter not of size or strength but of provident sense
coupling: the prudent wisdom that dwells in the humble and weak
reading: chakam (wise) — 'four things on earth are small, but they are exceedingly WISE' (30:24-28); wisdom is not a function of size or power. The ant's foresight, the badger's shelter, the locust's order, the lizard's boldness put the great to shame. The weak, provident, and orderly are wise (cf 6:6-8).
verse_text: Pro 30:24 Four things on earth are small , but they are exceedingly wise :

base_gloss: to establish: right; to establish: prepare; blow; to establish: establish; to establish: make; to establish: commit
read_sense_variants: forethought — the diligent readying for the day of battle | foresight — the ants storing food in summer against winter
sense: foresight — the ants storing food in summer against winter
operation: the ants' providing of their food in the summer — the provident foresight that, though the ants are weak, lays up in the time of plenty against the time of need, diligence and forethought outweighing strength
target: (the weakness it more than makes up for)
coupling: the forethought that provisions the future in the season of plenty
reading: kun (prepare/provide) — 'the ants are a people not strong, yet they PROVIDE their food in the summer' (cf 6:6-8); foresight and diligence, not strength, secure the future. The weak ant's provident planning is wisdom to be imitated. Emergent: provident forethought as the wisdom of the small.
verse_text: Pro 30:25 the ants are a people not strong , yet they provide their food in the summer ;

read_sense_variants: provident wisdom — the feeble badger securing its home in the rock
sense: provident wisdom — the feeble badger securing its home in the rock
operation: the rock badgers who, though not mighty, make their homes in the cliffs — the provident wisdom of the weak that compensates for want of strength by shrewd security, finding in the rock a refuge no strength could win
coupling: the shrewd wisdom that, lacking strength, secures itself in the safety of the rock
reading: atsum (mighty), negated — 'the rock badgers are a people not MIGHTY, yet they make their homes in the cliffs' (30:26); one of the four small-but-wise creatures (30:24). The feeble badger's wisdom is to build where no strength can reach it. Prudence compensates for weakness by choosing a sure refuge (cf 30:25).
verse_text: Pro 30:26 the rock badgers are a people not mighty , yet they make their homes in the cliffs ;

read_sense_variants: dignified confidence — the majestic, unhurried bearing of the assured
sense: dignified confidence — the majestic, unhurried bearing of the assured
operation: the stately tread of four creatures (lion, strutting cock, he-goat, and the king with his army) — the dignified, confident, unhurried bearing that comes of assurance and mastery, majesty expressed in how one carries oneself
coupling: the confident dignity that shows itself in an unhurried, majestic gait
reading: yatab (be good / stately) — 'three things are STATELY in their tread' (30:29-31); dignity of bearing — the lion unafraid, the king secure among his people — expresses inner assurance and mastery. A stately walk is confidence made visible.
verse_text: Pro 30:29 Three things are stately in their tread ; four are stately in their stride :

read_sense_variants: proud folly — vaunting oneself, to be stopped with silence
sense: proud folly — vaunting oneself, to be stopped with silence
operation: the folly of exalting oneself — the proud, foolish self-vaunting that, once recognised, calls for a hand clapped over the mouth, silence to halt the boasting before it does more harm
target: the evil-devising it is paired with (267251)
coupling: welded to the scheming of evil it is set beside
reading: nabal (be foolish) — 'if you have been FOOLISH, exalting yourself... put your hand on your mouth' (30:32); proud self-exaltation is folly to be stopped by silence. When caught vaunting oneself, the wise course is to shut the mouth (cf 17:28).
verse_text: Pro 30:32 If you have been foolish , exalting yourself , or if you have been devising evil , put your hand on your mouth .

read_sense_variants: malicious scheming — plotting evil, to be halted by silence
sense: malicious scheming — plotting evil, to be halted by silence
operation: the devising of evil — the malicious plotting that, like proud folly, should be halted by clapping a hand over the mouth, stopping the scheme before it becomes speech and deed
target: the self-exalting folly it is paired with (267248)
coupling: welded to the proud folly it is set beside
reading: zamam (devise/plot) — 'or if you have been DEVISING evil, put your hand on your mouth' (30:32); malicious scheming, like proud folly, is to be checked by silence — stop the plot before it hatches. Restraint of mouth restrains the evil (cf 30:33).
verse_text: Pro 30:32 If you have been foolish , exalting yourself , or if you have been devising evil , put your hand on your mouth .

read_sense_variants: provoked wrath — forcing anger, which inevitably yields strife
sense: provoked wrath — forcing anger, which inevitably yields strife
operation: the pressing/forcing of anger — the stirring and provoking of wrath that yields strife as surely as churning milk yields curds and a struck nose yields blood, anger pressed always producing conflict
coupling: welded to the conflict pressing anger produces
reading: aph (anger/nose, wordplay) — 'pressing ANGER produces strife' (30:33); as pressure on milk makes curds and on the nose makes blood, so pressing anger inevitably makes strife. Provoke wrath and conflict must follow — a reason to check the mouth (30:32).
verse_text: Pro 30:33 For pressing milk produces curds , pressing the nose produces blood , and pressing anger produces strife .

read_sense_variants: strife — which spoils a house of feasting | strife — honourably avoided | conflict — the strife a quarrelsome man sets ablaze | conflict — the inevitable yield of pressed anger
sense: conflict — the inevitable yield of pressed anger
operation: the strife that pressing anger produces — the conflict that follows as inevitably from provoked wrath as curds from churned milk, the guaranteed harvest of stirring up anger
target: the pressed anger that yields it (267264)
coupling: welded to the provoked wrath that produces it
reading: rib (strife) — 'pressing anger produces STRIFE'; strife is the certain product of provoked anger. Stir the wrath and the quarrel is assured (cf 15:18; 29:22).
verse_text: Pro 30:33 For pressing milk produces curds , pressing the nose produces blood , and pressing anger produces strife .

read_sense_variants: self-squandering lust — spending one's vigour on women, the ruin of kings
sense: self-squandering lust — spending one's vigour on women, the ruin of kings
operation: the giving of one's strength to women — the squandering of vigour and rule on sexual indulgence, the dissipation that has destroyed kings, a man's powers poured out on lust rather than kept for his calling
coupling: the vigour wasted on lust that has toppled kings
reading: chayil (strength/vigour) — 'do not give your STRENGTH to women, your ways to those who destroy kings' (31:3); Lemuel's mother warns against squandering one's powers on lust. Sexual indulgence has been the ruin of kings — strength spent there is strength lost from the throne (cf 5:9-11; 7:26).
verse_text: Pro 31:3 Do not give your strength to women , your ways to those who destroy kings .

read_sense_variants: forgetting — the adulteress's forgetting of the covenant of her God | forgetting — here forbidden: do not forget the teaching | forgetting — here forbidden: do not forget my words | intoxicated dereliction — drink making a ruler forget the law and pervert the poor's rights | compassionate relief — wine given the wretched to forget poverty and misery
sense: intoxicated dereliction — drink making a ruler forget the law and pervert the poor's rights
operation: the forgetting of what has been decreed through drink — the intoxicated dereliction by which a ruler loses hold of the law and perverts justice for the afflicted, wine drowning the judgement the weak depend on
coupling: the drink-drowned memory that fails the poor who look to the judge
reading: shakach (forget) — 'lest they drink and FORGET what has been decreed and pervert the rights of all the afflicted' (31:5); drink is perilous for rulers, drowning the memory of the law and corrupting justice for the weak. A judge in his cups fails the afflicted (cf 31:4).
verse_text: Pro 31:5 lest they drink and forget what has been decreed and pervert the rights of all the afflicted .

read_sense_variants: bitterness — the bitter aftertaste of the forbidden woman | anguish — the bitter distress that wine may ease
sense: anguish — the bitter distress that wine may ease
operation: the bitterness of soul of those in distress, to whom wine may bring relief — the deep anguish of the suffering and perishing, for whom drink is a mercy where for a ruler it is a peril
coupling: welded to the anguished soul it describes
reading: mar (bitter) — 'and wine to those in BITTER distress' (31:6); the anguish of the suffering, for whom wine is a comfort. What corrupts the judge (31:4-5) may mercifully ease the dying and the broken-hearted — drink judged by its use.
verse_text: Pro 31:6 Give strong drink to the one who is perishing , and wine to those in bitter distress ;

sense: suffering — the anguished soul given wine for relief
operation: the distress of soul of the perishing and heavy-hearted — the suffering spirit for whom strong drink is offered as a mercy, to help them forget their misery for a while
coupling: welded to the bitter anguish it feels
reading: nephesh (soul) — 'to those in bitter DISTRESS' (31:6, 'bitter of soul'); the anguished spirit of the suffering, for whom wine is a comfort. The same drink that endangers the ruler mercifully eases the perishing (cf Job 3:20).
verse_text: Pro 31:6 Give strong drink to the one who is perishing , and wine to those in bitter distress ;

read_sense_variants: forgetting — the adulteress's forgetting of the covenant of her God | forgetting — here forbidden: do not forget the teaching | forgetting — here forbidden: do not forget my words | intoxicated dereliction — drink making a ruler forget the law and pervert the poor's rights | compassionate relief — wine given the wretched to forget poverty and misery
sense: compassionate relief — wine given the wretched to forget poverty and misery
operation: the forgetting of poverty and misery that wine may bring the wretched — the compassionate relief offered the perishing and heavy-hearted, a mercy that lets the suffering lay down their grief for a while
coupling: the merciful oblivion granted the crushed and suffering
reading: shakach (forget) — 'let them drink and FORGET their poverty and remember their misery no more' (31:7); the same wine that endangers the ruler (31:4-5) is a mercy to the perishing, easing a grief too heavy to bear. Compassion, not indulgence, is the note here (cf 31:6).
verse_text: Pro 31:7 let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their misery no more .

read_sense_variants: just advocacy — speaking up and judging rightly for the voiceless
sense: just advocacy — speaking up and judging rightly for the voiceless
operation: the righteous judging and defending of the rights of the poor and needy — the just advocacy that opens its mouth for the voiceless, using power to secure justice for those who cannot secure it themselves
coupling: the righteous use of authority to protect the defenceless
reading: tsedeq (righteousness) — 'open your mouth, judge RIGHTEOUSLY, defend the rights of the poor and needy' (31:9); the crown of Lemuel's mother's counsel — power exists to protect the weak. Righteous rule speaks up for those who have no voice (cf 29:7, 14; 31:8).
verse_text: Pro 31:9 Open your mouth , judge righteously , defend the rights of the poor and needy .

sense: excellence — the capable wife, worth far more than jewels
operation: the excellence/valour of the capable wife whom the acrostic celebrates — the woman of strength and worth ('eshet chayil') who is far more precious than jewels, the sum of the virtues the poem unfolds
coupling: the strong, capable excellence that surpasses all price
reading: chayil (strength/valour/excellence) — 'an EXCELLENT wife who can find? She is far more precious than jewels' (31:10); 'eshet chayil' — a woman of valour, whose worth the whole acrostic (31:10-31) unfolds. Her excellence is a strength and capability beyond price (cf 12:4; Ruth 3:11).
verse_text: Pro 31:10 An excellent wife who can find ? She is far more precious than jewels .

read_sense_variants: trust — whole-hearted reliance on the LORD | misplaced trust — trusting in riches, which fails | trust — in the LORD, which is blessedness | God-reliance — the trust that is enriched | self-reliance — trusting one's own heart, which is folly | God-reliance — the trust that makes a man safe | reliability — the wife her husband's heart safely trusts
sense: reliability — the wife her husband's heart safely trusts
operation: the trustworthiness of the wife in whom her husband's heart can safely trust, so that he lacks no gain — the reliability and faithfulness that makes her a partner he can rest his confidence in wholly
target: (the husband's trusting heart that rests on her)
coupling: the dependable faithfulness that earns a husband's full confidence
reading: batach (trust) — 'the heart of her husband TRUSTS in her, and he will have no lack of gain' (31:11); her trustworthiness is such that her husband confides in her without reserve. Reliability of character is the foundation of the marriage's prosperity and peace.
verse_text: Pro 31:11 The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will have no lack of gain .

read_sense_variants: the good — the way the wise walk | the good — every good course the seeker discerns | good — the benefit owed to others, not to be withheld | good/well-regarded — the esteem gained | good — the sound worth of the precepts given | goodness — the good man who obtains favour | goodness — the good word that gladdens | goodness — the good quality of sound sense | goodness — the good man who leaves an inheritance | goodness — the good man filled with his own good fruit
sense: steadfast good — doing her husband good, never harm, all her days
operation: the doing of good and not harm to her husband all the days of her life — the steadfast, lifelong benevolence that seeks his welfare constantly, a goodness sustained not for a season but for a whole life
coupling: the constant, lifelong good-will that never turns to harm
reading: tob (good) — 'she does him GOOD, and not harm, all the days of her life' (31:12); her benevolence is lifelong and unwavering — not fitful kindness but a settled disposition to seek her husband's good always. Constancy of good-will marks her character.
